paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD opens this whole word with one sentence: "I have loved you," says the LORD (Malachi 1:2). Israel hears that and basically asks for receipts. I think a lot of us do the same thing, because it's easy to feel loved on a good day and wonder about it on a slow one.

So the LORD points them back to something He had done long before they asked. He reminds them of two brothers, and says, "Yet Jacob I have loved…" (Malachi 1:2). His love for Israel didn't start with their good behavior or their good week. It started with Him choosing them, and that means His love was already standing there before the question was even out of their mouths.

Then comes the heavy part, friend: the LORD says He has hated Esau, and when Edom talks about rebuilding, He says, "They may build, but I will demolish." (Malachi 1:4). He tells Israel they will see it with their own eyes and say, "The LORD is great…" (Malachi 1:5), even beyond the borders of Israel. He is not a small God with a small neighborhood, so when you doubt that you're loved, look at who is doing the loving. I got pulled out of a junk drawer by that kind of love, and I'm still baking on the planet He gave me.
